en.html:
Winter had been slow to come to Aizu this year.

The calendar already said winter. But the snow, which normally began whitening the trees and grass around the middle of the eleventh month, had not done so even once, though the twelfth had begun. Most unusual, our host had said.

Perhaps my luck was bad. A northern landscape ought, surely, to have its white snow before one judged it.

The mansion’s garden was splendid enough to show that its owners were a cadet branch of the great Ootori family. Even so, the dragon lacked its finishing eye.

The snow clouds waited at Aizu’s border.
Was it the direction of the winds above, or the ocean currents?

Or the blood-reeking heat given off by men crawling over the earth?

ja.html:
今年の会津は冬の訪れが遅い。

　暦の上では既に冬季である。
　しかし、例年通りならば霜月の中頃には降り始める
雪が、師走に入ってもまだ一度たりと草木を白く染め
ていない。珍しいことだと、家主は語っていた。

　不運なのかもしれない。そう思う。
　北国の景色は、やはり白雪の彩りを得て映えるもの
であろうから。

　屋敷内の庭園も名族大鳥家の<ruby>連枝<rt>れんし</rt></ruby>たるを示す見事な
ものではあったものの、何処か画竜点睛を欠く趣きは
否めない。

　雪雲は、会津の<ruby>國境<rt>くにざかい</rt></ruby>で足踏みしている。
　天の風向のためか海の潮流のためか。

　それとも地を這う人の発する血生臭い<ruby>熱<rt>いきれ</rt></ruby>のためか。

en.html:
With winter still unwhitened, the temperature too was falling gently. Born in the south and not raised in the north either, I seemed to have some time left before I froze under a kotatsu and could no longer bring myself to leave it.

In that time—


————What was to be done?

It was not for my judgment alone to decide.

en.html:
The old man spoke cheerfully, showing white teeth. The very picture of a kindly grandfather.

Nothing about him suggested the nerve to shelter someone hunted by an army as though it were no matter.
To make an enemy of this man by chance—troublesome would not begin to describe it.

en.html:
Kageaki"So those are the famous persimmons offered to the throne. To share the Emperor’s fare is a great honor."
永倉翁"If they have pleased you, I shall ask for another preparation at dinner. Now, our honored guest—"
永倉翁"Where would you be going? To Lady Kanae’s room, perhaps?"
Kageaki"Yes. That was my intention. If there is no objection, I would ask permission to visit her."
永倉翁"...Yes, I should think it is all right now. Only, spend a little time elsewhere first."
永倉翁"I do not think Lady Kanae has finished her lunch yet."
Kageaki"I see. ...Of course. Then I shall do as you advise."
永倉翁"After turning you away so often, now I make you wait again. My apologies."
Kageaki"Not at all. A visit that burdens the patient is no visit. I am grateful for each warning you gave me."
永倉翁"No, no, no. Put it like that, and you make me quite ashamed..."
Kageaki"I shall take a walk in your garden. Perhaps I hurried my meal; my stomach is a little uncomfortable. The walk can serve for digestion also."

景明 「あれが名高い献上柿。 　帝の御相伴に与れるとは光栄の至りです」
永倉翁 「気に入って頂けたなら、晩にはまた趣向を 変えて出してくれるよう言っておきましょう かの。 　して御客人」
永倉翁 「どちらに参られますのかな。 　もしや香奈枝様のお部屋へ？」
景明 「は。そのつもりでした。 　差し支えなくば、見舞いをお許し願いたく」
永倉翁 「……そうだの。もうよろしかろう。 　しかし、少々時間をつぶしてからになさり ませい」
永倉翁 「香奈枝様はまだ、昼餉を終えられておらぬ と思いますでの」
景明 「そうですか。……確かに。 　では、お勧めの通りに致します」
永倉翁 「何度も追い払った挙句にまた待ちぼうけを 食わせて、申し訳ございませぬ」
景明 「とんでもない。 　相手に迷惑を掛ける見舞いなど見舞いでは ありません。いちいちご忠告を下されたこと、 有難く思っております」
永倉翁 「いやいやいや。 　そのように言われては恐縮……」
景明 「御庭を歩かせて頂くことにしましょう。 　食事を急ぎ過ぎたのか、いささか胃の心地 が悪いので、腹ごなしも兼ねて」

en.html:
永倉翁"...Mm. Now you mention it, you were remarkably quick."
永倉翁"The family practice, is it?"
Kageaki"...No. Nothing of the sort. Normally I do not... Even just now, unusual speed in finishing was not something I had in mind."
永倉翁"Without putting your mind to it, then. The battlefield’s teaching coming out?"
Kageaki"............"
Kageaki"It may be so."
永倉翁"When the enemy may arrive at any moment, sitting over one’s food at leisure is almost a way of committing suicide. Naturally, the chopsticks must hurry."
永倉翁"But you need not be anxious here. Those occupation fellows surrounding this house... for the present, that is most unlikely."
Kageaki"Elder Nagakura, you mean—"
永倉翁"Our scouts returned a short while ago. According to them, that fellow Shishiku’s men have blocked the main routes across the border so closely, not even an ant could crawl out."
永倉翁"Nothing short of bringing up a great army will get through."
Kageaki"............"
永倉翁"Naturally, before very long such a situation will arise. But for a little while yet, you may put the worry aside."
Kageaki"Understood."

永倉翁 「……むふぅ。 　そういえば、随分とお早い」
永倉翁 「ご家風ですかな？」
景明 「……いえ。別段。 　普段はこのような事はなく……今とて殊更 迅速な完食を心掛けたわけではないのですが」
永倉翁 「では無意識に。 　戦場の心得が顕れましたのかな？」
景明 「…………」
景明 「そうかもしれません」
永倉翁 「いつ何時、敵に襲われるか知れぬとあらば、 食事にのんびり時間を掛けるなど自殺行為も 同然ですからのう。 　箸が早まるのは当たり前」
永倉翁 「しかし、ご案じ召されるな。 　当家が進駐軍の奴輩に取り巻かれるような 事は……当面、まずございますまいからの」
景明 「翁、それは」
永倉翁 「先刻、物見が戻って参りましてな。 　國境の要路は、獅子吼めの手勢で蟻の這い 出る隙間もなく固められているとの事」
永倉翁 「大軍を起こさねば、突破は叶いますまいて」
景明 「…………」
永倉翁 「無論のこと、そうした事態は遠からず出来しゅったい 致しましょうがの。 　今しばらくは、ご懸念に及ばず」
景明 「は」

en.html:
Old Nagakura’s words made me look back over the course of events, whether I wished to or not.
Yes—sooner or later, the occupation forces would pour into this Aizu.

That was the position we had reached.
